subject: Civil Engineering
title: Ready-Mix and Quality Control
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ready-Mix and Quality Control usable.

hook.text: A spinning drum on a truck keeps concrete mixed during the drive to the job site.

buildup.text: Ready-mix plants batch ingredients by computer — accuracy to the pound.

discovery.text: Concrete must be placed within 90 minutes of mixing — the clock starts at the plant.

twist.text: Cylinder tests at 7 and 28 days verify that delivered concrete meets the specified strength.

climax.text: If cylinders fail, the structure may need coring — drilling samples from the actual concrete.

punchline.text: You can't inspect concrete after it's placed. Test it before it hardens.

quiz.question: Why must ready-mix concrete be placed within 90 minutes?
options: The truck's fuel runs out after 90 minutes of driving
The hydration reaction progresses and the concrete begins to set, losing workability
Safety regulations limit the driver's time on the road

details.summary: Ready-mix concrete is batched at a central plant and delivered to construction sites in truck mixers, ensuring consistent quality through computerized batching, moisture monitoring, and continuous quality testing. It supplies over 75% of concrete used in construction in developed countries.
details.whyItMatters: Central batching with quality control systems produces far more consistent concrete than site-mixed alternatives. Quality assurance at the plant level protects structural integrity of finished construction.
takeaways: Computerized batching controls proportions to tolerances within 1 to 2%
Truck mixers maintain concrete workability during transport time
Quality testing includes slump, air content, temperature, and cylinder strength

faq.question: What quality tests are performed on ready-mix concrete at the job site?
faq.answer: Slump test verifies workability, air content test confirms freeze-thaw protection, and temperature measurement ensures proper curing conditions. Cylinder specimens are cast and tested at 7 and 28 days for compressive strength. Unit weight measurement confirms consistent batch composition.

faq.question: How long can ready-mix concrete be transported before it becomes unusable?
faq.answer: Most specifications require concrete to be placed within 90 minutes of batching, though this varies with temperature and admixture use. Hot weather accelerates setting so transport times may be limited to 60 minutes. Retarding admixtures can extend workable life to over two hours when needed.
